title: BlackRock's Larry Fink warns a data center moratorium could trigger a recession
key_facts: Larry Fink, CEO of BlackRock, spoke in a CNBC interview on Wednesday 14 Oct 2026.
He said 'a moratorium of some sort in this country' would put the US in a recession.
He called most fears about data center buildouts 'misinformation' and said 'Data centers are not the problem'.
Moody's estimates planned US data center capital spending at $700 billion this year, $2.4 to $2.48 trillion through 2030.
A Pew survey found at least 49% of Americans say data centers are mostly bad for the environment, home energy costs and quality of life nearby.
Fink also warned that the US national debt grew from $8 trillion in 2000 to $40 trillion in 2026.
quote_evidence: "So much of our economy is based on the buildout of this capex," Fink said.
He said "a moratorium of some sort in this country" would put the U.S. in a recession, commonly defined as two straight quarters of shrinking economic output.
why_it_matters_hint: Fink ties the economy's health to continued data center spending.
